subject: Animation
title: The Pixar-Disney Deal
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Pixar-Disney Deal.

hook.text: By 2004, Pixar had never made a flop. Disney's own animation studio had not had a hit in years.

buildup.text: Pixar's deal with Disney was expiring. Steve Jobs threatened to take Pixar to a rival distributor.

discovery.text: New Disney CEO Bob Iger realized losing Pixar would be catastrophic and proposed a full acquisition.

twist.text: Pixar's leaders demanded creative independence as a condition. Disney agreed to leave them alone.

climax.text: Disney bought Pixar for $7.4 billion in 2006 and put Ed Catmull in charge of all Disney animation.

punchline.text: The student bought the teacher and took over the school.

quiz.question: What condition did Pixar demand in the Disney acquisition?
options: That Disney shut down its own animation studio
Creative independence, with Disney agreeing not to interfere with Pixar's process
That all Disney films be made with CGI only

details.summary: Disney acquired Pixar for $7.4 billion in 2006, reuniting the companies after years of tension. Steve Jobs became Disney's largest individual shareholder, and Pixar leadership took creative control of Walt Disney Animation Studios, reshaping both organizations.
details.whyItMatters: The Pixar acquisition transformed Disney from a struggling animation studio into the dominant force in animated filmmaking. It also tested whether Pixar's creative culture could survive corporate absorption.
takeaways: Disney acquired Pixar for $7.4 billion in 2006
Pixar leadership took creative control of Walt Disney Animation Studios
The deal tested whether acquisition would preserve or destroy Pixar's culture

faq.question: Why did Disney need to acquire Pixar?
faq.answer: Disney Animation had failed to compete with Pixar's quality and was producing commercial disappointments. Meanwhile, the existing distribution deal was expiring and Pixar was exploring other partners. Disney bought Pixar to secure its creative output and fix their own struggling studio.

faq.question: How did the acquisition affect Pixar's creative culture?
faq.answer: Initially, Pixar's culture was protected and Pixar leaders improved Disney Animation. Over time, Disney's corporate priorities — sequels, streaming, merchandise — increasingly influenced Pixar's project selection. Whether Pixar's soul survived the acquisition remains debated.
